name: Elmadam
overview: Elmadam is a male figure mentioned in the genealogy of the Messiah as recorded in Luke 3:28. While his tribal affiliation and additional details are not specified, he holds significance as part of the ancestral line leading to Christ. No further notes elaborate on his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Elmadam is the sole name recorded for this individual, appearing in Luke 3:28. No specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to the name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Cosam as Elmadam's father, an inference drawn from the genealogical listing, and Er as his son, explicitly stated in Luke 3:28. Beyond these connections, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Elmadam's importance lies primarily in his place within the Messianic lineage, underscoring the fulfillment of God's promise through the generations leading to Jesus Christ. His presence in Luke's genealogy highlights the historical and theological continuity from Old Testament ancestry to the New Testament revelation of the Savior.
